title: Reimbursable Screening Services Program Extension Act of 2026
official_title: To authorize an extension and expansion of the reimbursable screening services program of the Transportation Security Administration, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Andrew Garbarino (R-NY) with 1 cosponsor. Cleared the House per the latest recorded action; no Senate action is recorded yet.
summary: Extends and expands the Transportation Security Administration's reimbursable screening services program by amending subsection (e) of section 225 of division A of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2019. The program's authorization runs "through fiscal year 2031" instead of "through fiscal year 2026," and the participation cap moves from "not more than eight" to "not more than 14."
brief: Extends TSA's reimbursable screening services program from fiscal year 2026 through fiscal year 2031 and raises the participation cap from eight to 14.

top_lines.headline: Program Extended Through FY2031
subs: Amends section 225(e) of division A of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2019 (49 U.S.C. 44901 note)

items.main: Names the Act the "Reimbursable Screening Services Program Extension Act of 2026".
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Extension and Expansion of Reimbursable Screening Services Program

items.main: Extension: amends subsection (e) of section 225 of division A of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2019 (Public Law 116-6; 49 U.S.C. 44901 note) by striking "through fiscal year 2026" and inserting "through fiscal year 2031."
items.detail: The five-year extension is the only change to the program's time horizon in this Act.

items.main: Expansion: further amends the same subsection (e) by striking "not more than eight" and inserting "not more than 14."
items.detail: The bill changes only that numeric cap; it does not further amend eligibility criteria in subsection (e).

gaps: The bill does not restate what the reimbursable screening services program does; that program is defined in the underlying section 225 of the 2019 appropriations act, which is not reproduced here.
The bill does not describe how the raised participation cap will be allocated among applicants or which entities are eligible.
The bill does not include a funding authorization or appropriation of its own.
The bill does not require any reporting to Congress on program utilization during the extended period.

modified: Section 225(e) of division A of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2019: authorization changed from "through fiscal year 2026" to "through fiscal year 2031"
Section 225(e) of division A of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2019: participation cap changed from "not more than eight" to "not more than 14"
